title: Left Rotate Array by One
statement:
Write a function that left-rotates an array `nums` by one position in-place and returns the modified array.

For example, if `nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, left rotating by one position results in `[2, 3, 4, 5, 1]`.

examples.explanation: All elements shift left by 1, and the first element goes to the end.
A single element remains the same after rotation.

editorial.approach: Store the first element in a temporary variable. Shift all other elements one index to the left: nums[i] = nums[i + 1]. Place the temporary element at the last index nums[n - 1].

hints: Store the first element `nums[0]` in a temporary variable.
Shift every other element one index to the left: `nums[i] = nums[i + 1]`.
Place the stored first element at the last index `nums[nums.length - 1]`.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Remove the first element using `.shift()` and push it to the end of the array using `.push()`.
bruteForceSolution.timeComplexity: O(n) (due to shifting elements in memory)

optimizedSolution.explanation: Store the first element. Shift all other elements one position to the left in a loop, then place the first element at the end.

interviewExplanation: Left rotating an array by one involves shifting all elements leftwards. While `.shift()` and `.push()` work in JS, shifting elements manually in a loop makes the O(n) array shift operation clear, running in O(1) auxiliary space.
